questions.q: What does `-E` add to `grep` that plain `grep` doesn't support without heavy escaping?
options: Extended regular expressions, like alternation (|) and quantifiers such as {2}
Automatic sorting of the output
Case-insensitive matching
The ability to search multiple files at once
questions.explain: grep -E enables extended regex syntax, allowing patterns like alternation and {n} quantifiers to be written directly instead of backslash-escaped.

questions.q: In `awk '{print $9}' access.log`, what does `$9` refer to?
options: The file's 9th byte
The 9th line of the file
A shell environment variable named 9
The 9th whitespace-separated field on the current line
questions.explain: awk automatically splits each line into fields by whitespace; $9 refers to the 9th such field on the current line, not a line number or byte offset.

questions.q: Why must `sort` run before `uniq -c` in a pipeline like `awk '{print $9}' | sort | uniq -c`?
options: uniq -c automatically sorts its input, so the order doesn't actually matter
Without sort, uniq -c would throw an error and refuse to run
uniq -c only collapses consecutive duplicate lines, so identical values must already be adjacent
sort is required to make awk's output valid
questions.explain: uniq only detects duplicates that are next to each other in the input. sort groups identical values together first so uniq -c can count them correctly.

questions.q: After `sort | uniq -c`, why is a second `sort -rn` added at the end of the pipeline?
options: To re-sort the count numbers produced by uniq -c, largest first, for a "top N" ranking
To remove duplicate counts
To alphabetize the unique values
It has no effect and is only there for readability
questions.explain: uniq -c's output is still ordered by value, not by count. sort -rn re-sorts numerically (-n) in reverse (-r) so the most frequent value appears first.

questions.q: `sed -E 's/^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/REDACTED/'` is applied to a log file. What does it do to each line?
options: Deletes the entire line if it starts with a number
Replaces a leading IPv4-style address at the start of the line with the literal text REDACTED
Sorts lines by their IP address
Counts how many IP addresses appear in the file
questions.explain: The sed substitution matches a leading dotted-number pattern (an IPv4 address) at the start of the line and replaces it with REDACTED, leaving the rest of the line unchanged.
